<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, run the MLA decode W_UV up-projection (`MLAAttention._v_up_proj`) on AITER's Triton bf16 batched GEMM when AITER has a tuned config for the layer's exact shape; otherwise keep `torch.bmm`. With the Kimi-K2.6 config from ROCm/aiter#6780 this speeds up Kimi-K2 / K2.5 / K2.6 decode at TP8 on MI355X.

All numbers below were measured with #61863 (now merged) applied to both the baseline and this PR; without it, Kimi-K2.6 takes the FP8 MLA prefill path, which produced wrong output (GSM8K 0.027 vs 0.93).

Requires AITER with ROCm/aiter#6780 (merged `c617bd42f2`, included in v0.1.27; the vLLM image bump is #63774).

## Claims

- Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4, TP8, MI355X: the decode W_UV GEMM drops from 9.1 µs to 5.0 µs per layer (hipBLASLt → AITER Triton), about 260 µs per decode step at 64 tokens.
- Serving: mean TPOT −3.0% at 1k/1k c=16, −2.2% at c=128 and −2.3% at 1k/8k c=64; at 1k/1k c=64, −3.4% with 256 prompts and +0.3% with 640 prompts.
- Same bf16 weights and math as `torch.bmm`; GSM8K and GPQA Diamond are unchanged within stderr.
- Only the W_UV kernel changes. Shapes AITER has no tuned config for keep `torch.bmm`.

## Validation

Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X (gfx950), AITER at `c617bd42f2`, ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`.

**Serving** (`vllm bench serve`, random, seed 0; 10 × concurrency prompts except where noted; this PR measured on a second pass of the same server, so Triton kernels are already compiled):

| ISL/OSL, conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean E2EL (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k, 16 | 1,597 → 1,622 (+1.5%) | 9.75 → 9.46 (−3.0%) | 10.26 → 10.10 (−1.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 64 (256 prompts) | 4,124 → 4,275 (+3.6%) | 14.71 → 14.21 (−3.4%) | 15.88 → 15.32 (−3.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 64 (640 prompts) | 4,256 → 4,234 (−0.5%) | 14.42 → 14.47 (+0.3%) | 15.40 → 15.47 (+0.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 128 | 6,372 → 6,507 (+2.1%) | 19.34 → 18.92 (−2.2%) | 20.56 → 20.14 (−2.1%) |
| 1k/8k, 64 | 4,032 → 4,128 (+2.4%) | 15.79 → 15.43 (−2.3%) | 130.0 → 127.0 (−2.3%) |

`vllm bench serve --model /data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len <1024|8192> --max-concurrency <c> --num-prompts <10*c> --ignore-eos --seed 0`

**Accuracy** (lm-eval):

| Task | Filter | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K, 5-shot | flexible-extract | 0.9386 ± 0.0066 | 0.9416 ± 0.0065 |
| GSM8K, 5-shot | strict-match | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | 0.9424 ± 0.0064 |
| GPQA Diamond CoT, 0-shot | flexible-extract | 0.7172 ± 0.0321 | 0.6818 ± 0.0332 |

GPQA strict-match is ~0.05 in both runs because its answer format doesn't match Kimi-K2.6's output, so it is omitted. The GPQA difference (−3.5 points, 7 of 198 questions) is within one standard error of the difference (~0.046).

**Kernel swap.** In rank-0 profiler traces of both versions, every step type that runs MLA decode changes only its 61 W_UV kernels per step (one per layer). W_UK and all other kernels are unchanged, and pure-prefill steps are kernel-for-kernel identical.

<details>
<summary>Per step type</summary>

| Step type | Before (hipBLASLt) | After (AITER Triton) | Per call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode, 64 tokens | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x64x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 16×32×256 (`M_LEQ_64`) | 9.14 → 4.97 µs |
| Decode, 32 tokens | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 16×32×256 (`M_LEQ_32`) | 8.00 → 4.53 µs |
| Decode, 1 token | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 32×32×256 (`M_LEQ_8`) | 7.03 → 4.23 µs |
| Prefill 32,767 + 1 decode token | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 32×32×256 (`M_LEQ_8`) | 9.64 → 4.06 µs |
| Prefill, 1,024 tokens | unchanged | unchanged | — |

</details>

**Tests**
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -v -k "v_up_proj or post_load"` on MI355X: `passed`
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports, torch.cuda and test-tethering checks pass.

## Details

- **Dispatch rule.** `rocm_aiter_ops.is_triton_bf16_bmm_tuned(B, M, N, K)` asks AITER's config lookup whether the exact shape has a tuned entry on the current GPU (cached per shape). It reuses `_triton_gemm_config_is_tuned`, which now takes optional `M` and `B`, and follows `is_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned`. There is no env var or model check; FP4/FP8 BMM still take precedence.
- **Scope with ROCm/aiter#6780.** The config is keyed on 8 heads (`B=8-N=128-K=512`), so it applies to the Kimi-K2 family at TP8, and to DeepSeek-V3 at TP16, which has the same per-GPU shape. AITER's lookup never reports an `any` entry as tuned, so the 16,384-token `any` config is not used: above 128 decode tokens W_UV stays on `torch.bmm`.
- **Safety.** `_v_up_proj` runs inside the MLA attention custom op, so torch.compile doesn't trace into the Triton call, and CUDA graphs capture it per batch size. It uses vLLM's existing strided views; there are no copies or weight changes.
- **Test.** `test_mla_v_up_proj_runs_tuned_aiter_triton_bf16_bmm` (ROCm only) uses a shape AITER already ships tuned gfx942/gfx950 configs for (N=1024, K=4096), so the real tuned lookup passes in CI without patching. It checks via the profiler that the AITER kernel ran, and compares against the `torch.bmm` path it replaces. Kimi's own shape needs the new AITER config, which the CI image may not have yet; it was validated on MI355X as above. The test reuses the existing hand-built `MLAAttention` setup in `test_mla_backends.py` (now a shared `_bare_mla_layer` helper) and runs in the MI355 V1 Attention step.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs searched for `batched_gemm_bf16`, `_v_up_proj` and AITER bf16 BMM: #53003 and #61926 use AITER's `batched_gemm_bf16` for DeepSeek-V4's einsum (a different call site); #36297 and #59856 fuse FP8 output quantization into `_v_up_proj`; #55741 refactors MLA BMM selection into an `MLABmm` abstraction without a Triton bf16 path. This change would fit #55741 as one more implementation.
- **Limitation.** "Tuned in AITER" is taken to mean faster than hipBLASLt. AITER's tuner compares Triton configs against each other, not against `torch.bmm`; for this shape it holds in every bucket exercised above.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the implementation, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
